clue.text: A pen's powers, none the less, might be seen in these publications

indicators.note: the remaining letters, rearranged, are what might be seen, so they are to be reworked into a new order
'less' means minus, so the letter that 'none' stands for is subtracted from the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written
none is nothing, which is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The proverbial mightiness of the pen shows in the daily press.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of A PEN'S POWERS and rearrange the rest to get NEWSPAPERS; the surface nods to 'the pen is mightier than the sword'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily papers are printed periodicals, the commonest kind of publication sold at a newsagent.

clue.text: Almost dark, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: A description of twilight, nearly dark yet not fully.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGHT loses its last letter to give NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old adverb meaning nearly, as in 'well nigh impossible'.

clue.text: Special brew in a drinking establishment

indicators.note: a special version is made differently, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub offering a special house beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a licensed venue serving mainly wine, so it is a place where people go to drink.

clue.text: Soldier with escort, perhaps — it's none of the government's business

definitions.text: it's none of the government's business

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is one possible arrangement of letters, so they may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier escorting someone, apparently on a matter that is none of the government's concern.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector comprises businesses owned privately rather than by the state, so its affairs are not state enterprise.

clue.text: Steals from place where secret is filed?

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
something is filed under a heading or letter
S is an abbreviation for secret

explanation.surface: A thief raids the place where confidential papers are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically: PL is filed UNDER S, which spells PLUNDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to rob or loot goods by force, so it means taking things from a person or place.

clue.text: Sculptor depicting river god

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: An artist carving a statue of a river deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French artist who made The Thinker and The Kiss in bronze and marble.

clue.text: Cat turned up a couple of seconds later

indicators.note: turned round means the following short word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
S is short for second; two of them come after

explanation.surface: A cat appeared a moment or two afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is an informal, affectionate word for a domestic feline, as in Puss in Boots.

clue.text: Experience release, securing some work

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: to undo a knot or fastening is to release it
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Being freed from prison while having some job lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through it or suffer it, which is what experiencing an event means.

clue.text: Minor thoroughfare that is surrounded by strange trees

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside the other piece of wordplay
something strange is oddly arranged, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
id est, Latin for that is, abbreviated as i.e.

explanation.surface: A little road lined by oddly shaped trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'that is' gives the Latin ID EST in full, not just its usual abbreviation IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A side street is a minor road branching off a main one, a lesser thoroughfare.

clue.text: Guardian spirits, in general (Roman ones)

parts.note: GEN is the abbreviation for general
I is one in Roman numerals; two of them

explanation.surface: A general remark about tutelary spirits, Roman ones in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genius, in the old Roman sense of a protective spirit attending a person or place.

clue.text: One is opened — see inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece of wordplay within the other

parts.note: to undo a door or parcel is to open it
vide is the Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Someone is opened up and told to look inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a pronoun but is the adjective meaning whole or united.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undivided is whole and unbroken, a single entity, which is the adjectival sense of one.

clue.text: Cruel group of people that perpetuates a problem

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: a situation that perpetuates a problem

parts.note: vicious means savage or cruel
a circle is a social set of people

explanation.surface: A cruel gang keeps a problem going.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is a chain of events where each difficulty causes another, so the trouble never ends.

clue.text: Eccentric lodgers? They're required to take off

definitions.meaning: a card is an eccentric person, and boarders lodge, so odd lodgers are cards who are boarding
the passes airline passengers must show before a flight departs

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: 'card' is British slang for an amusing oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline boarding passes are needed to get on a plane, which then takes off, and comically describe odd guests who board.

clue.text: Soldier runs in this, perhaps — an athlete's garment

parts.note: an old sweat is a veteran soldier

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the word that follows
perhaps signals one possible arrangement, so the combined letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A soldier might go jogging in this sporty top.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old sweat' is British slang for an experienced soldier; R goes into THIS, then those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose cotton jersey worn for sport and training, hence sportswear for athletes.

clue.text: Cautious about damage, having had too much conflict

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: wary means careful or cautious
wear is damage from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about damage after enduring too much fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: War-weary describes people exhausted by prolonged fighting, tired of strife and battle.

clue.text: Knave, for example, to be found among thieves?

definitions.meaning: in card games such as bridge, the knave or jack is one of the top-ranking court cards
the proverb says there is this quality even among crooks

explanation.walkthrough: A knave is also a rogue, so the surface seems to be about villains; the second part echoes the saying 'honour among thieves'.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are called honours, and the proverb credits criminals with integrity.

clue.text: English poet composed sonnet about US city

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap the abbreviation
a composed piece has been put together, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A poet writes a sonnet about an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote In Memoriam and The Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: What you need to do

parts.note: surface reading: a vague instruction about one's duties
setter's reading: what a solver must do to this very clue

explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: the solver's task is to respond to each clue with the right word.
explanation.definitionFit: Responding correctly to a question or puzzle is exactly what every solver has to accomplish here.

clue.text: Peak after fall in shares now capitalised

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the third, with the middle word whole

explanation.surface: Stock market talk: a high point reached after a slump once shares are capitalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like a market drop but means a snowfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcap is the white covering left on a mountain top once snow has come down.

clue.text: As belief gets changed, it's not ruled out

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: As opinion shifts, a possibility remains open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something workable or possible remains a viable option, so it has not been dismissed or excluded.

clue.text: Sheep delivered around middle of night

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps the selected letters

parts.note: a baby that is delivered is born

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, not its ends

parts.note: the inner three letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lamb arriving at midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The bighorn is a wild North American mountain sheep with huge curling horns.

clue.text: Brief film about execution for dishonest behaviour

parts.note: a short is a brief film
C is circa, Latin for about
hanging is a form of execution

explanation.surface: A short movie about a hanging, made to depict wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-changing is cheating someone by giving too little change, a form of swindling.

clue.text: House briefly reflected on a disturbance

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the same two-letter abbreviation as seen in a mirror, back to front
on means next to, and a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of the House reflecting on a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: HO is followed by its mirror image OH, then A, giving HOO-HA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal British word for a fuss or commotion over something trivial.

clue.text: Burden of daily round lifted

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A paper boy's daily delivery round becomes a weight lifted off.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is a responsibility or obligation, a duty one must carry like a load.

clue.text: Be subject to promises to repay, without interest

parts.note: to incur a penalty is to become subject to it
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Debtors bound by IOUs, which happen to charge no interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial, fitting the debt picture, but means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Incurious means lacking curiosity, showing no wish to know about things.

clue.text: Top flier going directly north

parts.note: 'as the crow flies' means by the most direct route
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A top pilot heading straight northward.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the topmost part of the head, a hat or a hill.

clue.text: Character fault concealed by crafty politician

indicators.note: concealed by says the letters lie hidden within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cunning politician hides a flaw in his personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character fault' suggests a personal failing; here a character is a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing error, a mistake in a single letter or symbol.

clue.text: For which opponents must go to court (it's not hard)

definitions.text: For which opponents must go to court (it's not hard)

parts.words: For which opponents must go to court
parts.note: surface reading: adversaries in a lawsuit heading to a court of law
setter's reading: a racket game played on grass rather than a hard court

explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests litigation; the bracket points to a grass surface, as opposed to a hard court.
explanation.definitionFit: The full traditional name of the racket sport, originally played on grass courts, as at Wimbledon.
